subject: Mystic Shoreline Initiative and West Medford History
overview: The center hosted a presentation on the Mystic Shoreline Initiative followed by a jazz-poetry performance by the Ally Project exploring neighborhood legacy and social justice.

items.title: Introduction and Environmental Discussion
items.summary: Terry Carter introduced Shannon Collins of the Mystic River Watershed Association and performed poetry addressing the gentrification and environmental evolution of the Mystic River area.

items.title: Mystic Shoreline Initiative and Flood Resilience
items.summary: Collins detailed the Mystic Shoreline Initiative, which uses resident feedback to design ADA-accessible stone-dust paths, improved river overlooks, and safer pedestrian crossings near local rotaries. The discussion also addressed a new stormwater resilience project intended to collect resident accounts of street-level flooding and drainage issues for future infrastructure planning.

items.title: Performance: The Ally Project
items.summary: The Ally Project quartet performed jazz-poetry compositions reflecting on the historical Black presence in the 'Ville' neighborhood and the impacts of property redevelopment. The performance featured original works honoring local landmarks such as the 'Little Store' on Jerome Street and the former Shiloh Baptist Church.

items.title: Community Announcements
items.summary: Staff shared upcoming center updates including the organization's 90th-anniversary celebrations, a May screening of a documentary about Black Revolutionary War patriots, and a scam prevention workshop for elders.
